contributions.anchor: Column A 'Total this Period' TOTAL CONTRIBUTIONS RECEIVED (17,959.92) on the p2 SUMMARY PAGE, which is also the filer's own printed 'Total Contributions Received (sum of subtotals from all Schedule A pages): $ 17,959.92' at the foot of p6
contributions.detail: Three-anchor closure. The 69 rows of the filer's own typed ledger sum by page to its OWN printed page subtotals: p4 30 rows = 9,574.92 = printed 'Subtotal for this page: $ 9,574.92'; p5 30 rows = 6,900.00 = printed 6,900.00; p6 9 rows = 1,485.00 = printed 1,485.00. 9,574.92 + 6,900.00 + 1,485.00 = 17,959.92 = the ledger's own printed grand total AND the cover's PROMOTED per-period cell, Column A line 1 (17,959.92), AND summary line 4 'Total Contributions Received (From Line 1 Column A)' 17,959.92. EXACT to the cent on every anchor. Column B 'Year-to-Date Total' prints the SAME 17,959.92 and is not summed as an increment — this is the cycle's FIRST report (line 3 Balance at Beginning is an oval zero), so period IS year-to-date, which is the Ratcliffe pattern of addendum C2 and not an anomaly. The three in-kind rows (100.00 + 1,795.00 + 2,000.00 = 3,895.00) are INSIDE that 17,959.92 — see in_kind_convention.

expenditures.anchor: Column A 'Total this Period' TOTAL EXPENDITURES MADE (15,138.48) on the p2 SUMMARY PAGE, which is also the filer's own printed 'Total Expenditures (sum of subtotals from all Schedule B pages): $ 15,138.48' at the foot of p9
expenditures.detail: Three-anchor closure. The 53 rows sum by page to the filer's own printed page subtotals: p8 30 rows = 9,283.45 = printed 'Subtotal for this page: $ 9,283.45'; p9 23 rows = 5,855.03 = printed 5,855.03. 9,283.45 + 5,855.03 = 15,138.48 = the ledger's printed grand total AND the cover's Column A line 2 AND summary line 6 'Total Expenditures Made (From Line 2 Column A)' 15,138.48. EXACT. Column B YTD prints the same 15,138.48 (first report of the cycle) and is never summed as an increment. The cover's ladder also closes independently: line 3 balance-at-beginning 0 + line 4 17,959.92 = line 5 subtotal 17,959.92, minus line 6 15,138.48 = line 7 balance at close 2,821.44, exactly as printed. The three in-kind rows (3,895.00) are inside the 15,138.48 as well.

in_kind_convention: MONETARY-PLUS-IN-KIND, both sides — tested and the ONLY convention that closes. The filer marks three gifts '(in-kind donation)' inside the NAME/VENDOR cell (Ronald Nathan Ivie 100.00 · Stone Gate 1,795.00 · Reagan Outdoor Advertising 2,000.00 = 3,895.00) and books EACH ONE TWICE — once as a contribution and once as an offsetting expenditure of the identical amount and date. Both stated Column A figures INCLUDE them: monetary-only would give 14,064.92 against a stated 17,959.92 and 11,243.48 against a stated 15,138.48, i.e. 3,895.00 short on each side. This filer therefore does NOT follow the family's cash-only default (CHUNK_BRIEF §3), which is exactly the per-filer variation the brief requires be tested rather than inherited. There is no separate printed in-kind line anywhere on this filing.
